title: 19 In Vitro true digestibility and fat composition of whole cottonseed
content:
Abstract
Whole cottonseed is a widely used feed component in beef cattle nutrition, valued for its unique combination of fiber, energy, and protein. This makes it a cost-effective and energy-dense feed option particularly suitable for growing and finishing beef cattle. The high fat content in whole cottonseed effectively increases dietary energy density, contributing to improved weight gain and feed efficiency. However, the high fat and fiber content can pose challenges, as excessive fat may disrupt rumen microbial activity leading to reduced fiber digestion and nutrient availability. Careful formulation and ration balancing are necessary to optimize the inclusion of whole cottonseed in the diet while minimizing potential negative effects on ruminal fermentation and overall animal performance. This study evaluated the relationship between crude fat content and in vitro true digestibility across 772 cottonseed samples and examined variability in these traits among varieties over two years. Samples were sent to a commercial laboratory (Cumberland Valley Analytical Services, Waynesboro, PA, USA) for determination of crude fat concentration measured via the ether extract method. In vitro true digestibility was measured using the ANKOM DaisyII incubator. Crude fat concentration ranged from 10.9% to 29%, with an average of 22.1%, while in vitro true digestibility ranged from 48.5% to 63.1%, averaging 56.5%. There was no correlation (r = 0.38) between crude fat content and in vitro true digestibility. Our findings highlight the variability in crude fat and digestibility among cottonseed varieties and suggest that factors other than fat content may influence digestibility. The variability observed among cottonseed varieties highlights the importance of selecting cottonseed varieties tailored to meet specific nutritional goals for cattle. Further research is needed to identify the underlying factors affecting digestibility to optimize the use of whole cottonseed in cattle diets. Strategies such as genetic selection could enhance its potential in beef cattle diets.
